title: Inventory Mismatch Handling
text: An inventory mismatch exists when system stock differs from the physically counted shelf stock for a store and SKU. Log an Inventory Mismatch exception as soon as a count differs from the system value.

title: Inventory Mismatch Handling
text: Recount the SKU at its shelf location, check recent returns and stock adjustments, and record the counted quantity. If the difference is confirmed, prepare a stock adjustment for review before the system value is changed.

title: Inventory Mismatch Handling
text: If the same SKU shows a mismatch more than once in a shift, escalate to the Fulfillment Manager. A stock adjustment that requires approval stays in Pending Approval until a manager records a decision.

title: Stockout and Short-Pick Handling
text: A stockout is recorded when an order line is picked short because the shelf holds fewer units than ordered. Log a Stockout exception against the order and the SKU.

title: Stockout and Short-Pick Handling
text: Confirm the shelf count, pick the units that are available, and mark whether a substitution was offered. Do not pick from another SKU unless a substitution has been recorded for the order line.

title: Stockout and Short-Pick Handling
text: Repeated stockouts on the same SKU are reported to the Fulfillment Manager for a replenishment check. Record the action taken before the exception is closed.

title: Picking Delay Response
text: A picking delay is raised when picking for an order runs longer than 10 minutes. In this prototype the 10-minute value is a synthetic generation assumption, not a validated rule.

title: Picking Delay Response
text: Check the picker workload, the number of lines in the order, and any stock problems at the shelf. Move the order to a free picker where possible and note the likely cause.

title: Picking Delay Response
text: If the delay will push the order toward its promised time (30 minutes in this prototype), flag the order to the Fulfillment Manager so the downstream stages can be prepared.

title: Packing Delay Response
text: A packing delay is raised when packing for an order runs longer than 6 minutes. The value is a synthetic generation assumption.

title: Packing Delay Response
text: Check for packing material shortages, an item that needs re-checking, or a packing station backlog. Record any packing issue so it can be reviewed later.

title: Packing Delay Response
text: Draft guidance: when several packing delays occur in the same hour, the manager may re-balance packing staff between stations. This section is not yet approved.

title: Rider Shortage and Assignment Delay Response
text: A rider assignment delay is raised when a packed order waits more than 5 minutes for a rider. The value is a synthetic generation assumption.

title: Rider Shortage and Assignment Delay Response
text: Check how many riders are available, busy or unavailable for the store. Hold the order at the dispatch point and keep the packed order protected from handling delays.

title: Rider Shortage and Assignment Delay Response
text: If no rider is available, notify the Delivery Operations Manager. Any decision to bring in additional riders is taken by the manager and recorded against the exception.

title: Delivery Delay Response
text: A delivery delay is recorded when an order is delivered after its promised time, or is still undelivered once that time has passed. The cause may sit in an earlier stage.

title: Delivery Delay Response
text: Trace the order back through picking, packing and rider assignment to find the earliest stage that deviated. Record the likely cause as a candidate cause, not as a confirmed fact.

title: Delivery Delay Response
text: Older version 1.0 of this guidance asked associates to phone the customer for every delay. It has been replaced by version 2.0 and is retired.

title: SLA At Risk and Breach Response
text: In this prototype an order is At Risk when it is not yet delivered and no more than 10 minutes remain before its promised time. It is Breached when the promised time has passed without delivery. These are synthetic assumptions.

title: SLA At Risk and Breach Response
text: Open the order detail, review the current stage and the time spent in it, and check related exceptions. Prioritise the stage that is holding the order.

title: SLA At Risk and Breach Response
text: Record the decision taken for an At Risk or Breached order. Where the action needs human approval, the exception waits in Pending Approval until a manager decides.

title: Failed Delivery Attempt Handling
text: A failed delivery attempt is recorded when the rider cannot hand the order to the customer. The delivery stays open and the failed attempt is logged.

title: Failed Delivery Attempt Handling
text: In this prototype the rider makes at most one retry. Contact the customer through the approved channel, note the reason for the failure and record the retry time.

title: Failed Delivery Attempt Handling
text: If the retry also fails, the order is marked Delivery Failed and the Delivery Operations Manager decides on the next step. The decision is recorded on the exception.

title: Exception Logging and Approval Guidelines
text: Every operational exception is logged with a category, the affected order or store, and the time it was detected. Use the category list that is currently in use; it is a proposal and may change.

title: Exception Logging and Approval Guidelines
text: An exception moves through Open, Under Investigation, Pending Approval where an approval is needed, and Resolved/Closed. Record the resolution in plain words before closing.

title: Exception Logging and Approval Guidelines
text: Whether an action requires approval is decided by store management. Where approval applies, the approver records Approved, Edited or Rejected together with the time of the decision.

title: Peak Hour Operating Guidelines
text: Peak hours are the busiest order periods of the day, typically around midday and in the evening in this synthetic scenario. Plan staffing and rider cover before they start.

title: Peak Hour Operating Guidelines
text: Draft guidance: stagger breaks for pickers and packers and keep a rider on standby near the dispatch point. This section is still under review.

title: Peak Hour Operating Guidelines
text: During peak hours check the dashboard for orders that are At Risk and for open exceptions at least once every few minutes.

title: Shift Handover Checklist
text: At the end of a shift the outgoing associate lists open exceptions, orders still in progress and any stock problems found during the shift.

title: Shift Handover Checklist
text: The incoming associate reads the list, confirms who owns each open exception and asks about anything unclear before starting work.

title: Shift Handover Checklist
text: Handover notes are kept in the shift log. Open exceptions that are Pending Approval are named to the manager on duty.

title: Order Cancellation Handling
text: An order may be cancelled before picking starts. A cancelled order has no picking, packing or delivery record and is not measured against its promised time.

title: Order Cancellation Handling
text: Older guidance allowed cancellation after packing had started. This guidance is no longer used and has been retired.

title: Order Cancellation Handling
text: Record the cancellation time and the reason. If stock was reserved for the order, release it so that the shelf count stays accurate.
